data.name: Usage
data.value:
Debloater.Cli - testing and automation for the tweak catalog
Usage: Debloater.Cli list [--category X] [--catalog DIR] Debloater.Cli status [--category X] [--catalog DIR] [--verbose] Debloater.Cli apply <id...> [--max-risk low|medium|high|critical] [--catalog DIR] Debloater.Cli revert <id...> [--catalog DIR] Debloater.Cli validate [--catalog DIR] [--reference [--admx-dir DIR] [--csp FILE] [--warnings-out FILE]]
Debloater.Cli inventory [--kind K[,K...]] [--uncatalogued] [--json] Debloater.Cli inventory snapshot <file.json> [--kind K] Debloater.Cli inventory diff <old.json> <new.json> [--json]
Debloater.Cli admx list [--search TEXT] [--configured] [--admx-dir DIR] Debloater.Cli admx show <[File.admx:]Name> [--admx-dir DIR] Debloater.Cli admx export <file.json> [--with-state] [--admx-dir DIR]
Debloater.Cli policy show <[File.admx:]Name> [--scope machine|user] [--state S [--value id=value]...] Debloater.Cli policy set <[File.admx:]Name> --state enabled|disabled|notconfigured [--value id=value]... [--scope machine|user] [--dry-run] [--max-risk high] Debloater.Cli policy revert <[File.admx:]Name> Debloater.Cli policy backups
Debloater.Cli reference annotate [--write] [--force] [--admx-dir DIR] [--csp FILE]
Debloater.Cli catalog info | update [--check-only] | rollback [--previous] Debloater.Cli catalog verify <catalog-V.zip> <catalog-V.zip.sig> Debloater.Cli catalog pack --out DIR [--bundle-version V] [--key-env NAME]
Debloater.Cli fingerprint create <out.json.gz> [--root C:\] [--binaries default|all|none] Debloater.Cli fingerprint diff <old.json.gz> <new.json.gz> [--md R.md] [--json R.json] [--top 100] [--no-privacy]
Debloater.Cli selftest [--id ID]... [--category X] [--max-risk R] [--include-irreversible] [--json REPORT.json] [--backup-dir DIR] [--restore-point] [--verbose] [--phase full|apply-only|verify|revert] [--state STATE.json] [--label LABEL] [--i-know-this-is-not-a-vm]
--lang L (any command) interface language: en, en-US, pt, pt-BR or auto (default: auto = the Windows display language). Also selects the ADML language of admx/policy/validate. --category X filters by category prefix, as an identifier or as displayed (e.g. privacy, "System/Scheduled tasks"). --max-risk maximum risk accepted by 'apply' (default: medium). High/Critical require an explicit opt-in. --catalog DIR catalog folder (default: the active catalog: the newest verified update in %LocalAppData%\Debloater\catalog, or 'catalog' next to the executable). --kind K services, drivers, tasks, appx, features, capabilities, autoruns, featureflags. --admx-dir DIR PolicyDefinitions folder (default: C:\Windows\PolicyDefinitions). Accepts the latest Administrative Templates package downloaded from Microsoft. --csp FILE Policy CSP reference (default: reference/msdocs-policy-csp.json in the repository). fingerprint fingerprint of an installation (inventory, ADMX, registry/policy strings in binaries) and diff between builds, with new tweak candidates. Read-only. --root DIR (fingerprint create) installation root (default: C:\). Another folder = mounted image (offline: only the file-based parts). --binaries M (fingerprint create) default = curated list of relevant binaries; all = every PE under the roots; none = no binary scan. --md / --json (fingerprint diff) writes the Markdown / JSON report (with the "candidates" list). No report is written unless a path is given (keep reports out of git, e.g. under .claude/docs/). --top N (fingerprint diff) candidates in the Markdown table (default: 100). --no-privacy (fingerprint diff) turns off the privacy filter (on by default; --privacy turns it on): omits third-party/hardware/separately installed items, what only existed on the old PC without evidence of being part of Windows, and the machine names. policy configures an ADMX policy by writing directly to the registry (HKLM/HKCU\...\Policies), backing up the original value in %ProgramData%\Debloater\backups\policies. --value repeats per item (list/multiText); list with name=value: --value Id=name=value. Enum accepts the value, the display name or #index; boolean true/false. --dry-run only shows the preview. High risk (security/Update/Defender) requires --max-risk high. Does not change Registry.pol: gpedit.msc does not show what was written. apply/revert/policy set/policy revert require an administrator prompt. The other commands are read-only.
selftest DISPOSABLE VM ONLY: for each tweak, reads the state, applies, checks (Applied), re-applies (the original backup must stay intact), reverts and checks that each action went back to its previous value. Refuses to run outside a Hyper-V guest unless --i-know-this-is-not-a-vm is passed. Requires administrator. Default: all tweaks, all risks; irreversible ones (appx) only with --include-irreversible. --id ID tweak to test (repeatable or comma-separated). --json FILE (selftest) writes the JSON report, updated after each tweak. --backup-dir DIR (selftest) backup folder (default: %ProgramData%\Debloater\backups). --restore-point (selftest) creates a restore point first and records the result. --phase P (selftest) phased persistence test: apply-only applies and writes the state file; verify re-reads the state and reports which tweaks Windows undid (repeatable, with --label, e.g. after a reboot and after waiting); revert reverts and compares with the original state. Default: full (whole cycle at once). --state FILE (selftest) phase state file (default: %ProgramData%\Debloater\selftest-state.json). --label TEXT (selftest --phase verify) label of the check (default: verify-<n>).

data.name: CatalogUsage
data.value: Usage: catalog info active catalog (built-in or updated), versions, last check catalog update [--check-only] downloads, verifies and activates a newer signed catalog catalog rollback [--previous] back to the built-in catalog (or to the previous update) catalog verify <zip> <sig> checks a bundle's signature, manifest and compatibility catalog pack --out DIR [--catalog DIR] [--reference-dir DIR] [--bundle-version V] [--git-commit SHA] [--min-app-version V] [--key-env NAME | --key FILE.pem] builds catalog-V.zip, manifest.json and latest*.json; with a key (PEM in an environment variable or file) also signs it (.sig)
